title: What you have not seen
standfirst: The country members return to most, which means the work is in finding what is left.

blocks.heading: A house, a driver, one region
paras: Most members arriving in Italy have already done the cities. What they have not usually done is stay still in one region for ten days with a house and a cook.
We plan Italy by valley and by table, not by itinerary, and we keep the driver for the whole stay rather than by the day.

blocks.heading: Out-of-hours access
blocks.caption: Galleries and chapels before or after public hours.
paras: Almost every significant collection in Italy can be opened privately outside public hours, for a fee and with enough notice.
We arrange these months ahead, which is the difference between seeing a fresco and queueing for one.

blocks.heading: The table is the point
blocks.caption: A long lunch, booked long before arrival.
paras: The restaurants worth travelling for take bookings weeks out and do not answer email in August.
We hold the tables before the house is confirmed, because the tables are harder to get.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: April to June and September to October. August belongs to the mountains, not the cities or the coast.
Over five nights, a house with staff, every time. Under five, a hotel is simpler and the difference is small.
In the countryside, yes. Parking in the hill towns is the single most tiring part of an Italian holiday.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
